# property registry SET — same RPC as GET (excerpts)
# Evidence: registry SET 0x60192d30 (single caller 0x6016a208, the state-1 branch of
# the SET wrapper 0x6016a150 which has ~200 callers from the charger stack with the id
# passed dynamically in a register): arg checks (ptr != 0, type <= 4, size <= 4) ->
# the SAME registry lookup 0x60192f40 (match by table_ptr, lock, fetch) -> masked
# value merge out = (out & mask) | (new & ~mask) -> 0x601933f0 -> RPC cmd 0x107 via
# 0x6012b138 (call site 0x6019388c, payload: word0 = table_ptr, +4 = size, +8 = 7).
# => GET and SET share one RPC command; a SET of 0x270b via a dynamic id is possible
# in principle but statically invisible (no 0x270b immediate on any SET path; all six
# visible 0x270b references in the firmware are GETs).
